QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_30

question.text: Under SAS-400, Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA CA) observes that the SE employs 180 women out of 300 staff (60%). Which metric best captures GENDER-EQUALITY IMPACT rather than just representation?

answer.text: Female representation at managerial / decision-making layer AND pay-parity AND retention / progression (not just bottom-layer headcount)

explanation.text: The Logic: A meaningful gender-equality indicator must measure representation THROUGH the hierarchy plus pay-parity plus retention/promotion rates — not just headcount at the bottom. 60% headcount with zero women managers is not gender equality. The Trap: Options A, C, B are distractors — headcount alone can mislead, staff cost is financial, age is demographic. Cross-Exam Context: Representation-at-layers logic aligned with SEBI BRSR (III-A / III-C Compliance) and diversity-disclosure in XV Research Analyst. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Break down the workforce into at least 3 layers (entry / mid / senior management) with female % at each — this single chart reveals the real diversity story in 5 seconds.
